detail.description: Human-readable detail. Never contains a secret.

Bookmark.description:
One channel's bookmark and the revision it is at. `#240 reading-bookmark`.

`anchor` is `null` when no bookmark is set, which is a different answer from the field being
absent on a read: absent means the server could not say. The revision is `0` for a channel that
never had one, and otherwise only grows (through [`next_pin_revision`]), so a page can send it
back as `if_revision` and be refused when another device moved the bookmark since.

anchor.description: Where it is, or `null` when there is none.

BookmarkAnchor.description:
Where one channel's bookmark is: next to which message, on which side, and enough about that
message to draw the line in a list that does not hold it. `#240 reading-bookmark`.

`timestamp` and `thread_id` are copied from the message as the page was served it, so Main can
place the line for a thread reply it never shows, by time. Ids and an instant, and no text: a
bookmark is not a second copy of anybody's words.

message_id.description: The message the line is drawn next to, in the provider-neutral namespace it was served in.

place.description: Which side of that message the line is on.

thread_id.description: The thread that message is in, when it is in one.

timestamp.description: When that message was sent, ISO-8601, exactly as the provider reported it.

BookmarkPlace.description: Which side of its message a bookmark is on. `#240 reading-bookmark`.

oneOf.description: Just above the message: "start reading here". The usual case, and what setting one makes.

Just below it. Only when the newest message has been marked Done with the line on it, so the
line ends up under every message there is and above whatever arrives next.

BookmarkResponse.description:
One channel's bookmark, read or written: `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/channels/{id}/bookmark`.
`#240 reading-bookmark`.

A conditional write that lost to a move made elsewhere answers 409 with this same body and an
[`ApiErrorBody`]'s two fields beside it, so the page takes where the bookmark is now from the
refusal itself.

bookmark.description: The bookmark as stored after the call.

bookmark_notice.description: The standing statement that the bookmark is this server's own and marks nothing read.

changed.description: Whether the call changed what is stored: false for a read, a repeat, and a refusal.

ChannelId.description: A Discord channel snowflake, as a string, exactly as Discord renders it.

ChannelInfo.description: A channel this server is configured to read.

added.description:
Whether this channel was added from inside the app rather than named in the configuration
file.

The page needs it to say what Remove will do. Removing an added channel forgets it. A
configured one comes from a file this server reads and never writes, so removing it HIDES
it instead — the file still names it, and Settings can show it again. `#199
removable-config-channels`.

alias.description:
The operator's own local name for this channel, when he has set one. `#39 channel-alias`.

**Local, and only ours.** It lives in this server's store, exactly as read state does; it
is never sent to Discord, renames nothing there, and no one outside this deployment sees
it. It is set by the OPERATOR through the web app — never by the voice agent, which would
otherwise be renaming the things it is also reporting on.

`None` means "no alias", which is not the same as an empty one: an empty alias is refused
at the door, and clearing an alias is a separate act that puts [`ChannelInfo::label`] back.

It is `None` on a channel that came straight from [`crate::config::Config`]; the store
overlay in [`crate::ops`] is what fills it in, so anything reading configuration directly
— the startup banner, the preflight probe — still names the label the operator wrote.

label.description:
Human label used in speech and in the web app ("acme lead team").

This one comes from the operator's CONFIGURATION file and cannot be changed at runtime.
What a person actually hears is [`ChannelInfo::display_name`], because `#39 channel-alias`
lets him rename a channel from inside the app without editing a file or redeploying.

provider.description:
Key of the configured chat provider this channel is read through.

A deployment may serve several providers at once, and the page needs to know which one a
channel belongs to in order to describe it and to use only that provider's capabilities.
Absent only from an older server, which had exactly one provider.

writable.description: Whether posting into this channel is permitted at all.

ClientConfigResponse.description: What the web app needs to know at startup.

channel_discovery_supported.description: Whether the selected provider can list its channels for browsing. `#19 channel-browser`.

channel_registration_supported.description: Whether the selected provider accepts channel links or references and manages registration.

chat_provider_name.description: Source chat service's human-readable name, supplied by the selected backend.

conversational_voice.description: Selected conversational voice provider, named by its implementation.

elevenlabs_agent_id.description:
ElevenLabs agent id, when the deployment has one. Not a secret: it identifies a public
widget. The API key never leaves the server.

hidden_channels.description:
Channels from the configuration file the owner took off his list, in configuration order.
`#199 removable-config-channels`.

Settings lists them so each can be shown again; `channels` above already leaves them out.
Sent only to a write-scope caller, because showing one again takes that scope and a
read-scope credential has no use for the names of channels the owner put away. Absent when
none are hidden, and from an older server, which could not hide one.

idempotent_posts_supported.description:
Whether a post sent again under the same `idempotency_key` is posted at most once.

`#195 send-resilience`. The page retries a send whose answer it lost — a timeout, a 502 —
on its own only when this is true, because only then can the retry not post the message
twice. Sent only when true: absent, from this server or an older one, means false.

live_delivery.description: How changes reach the SSE hub.

live_poll_seconds.description:
Seconds between live ingestion ticks, or `0` when live ingestion is OFF.

The page needs this to tell the truth about its own channel view. With ingestion off the
SSE stream attaches and delivers nothing, which is indistinguishable from a quiet channel;
a page that showed a "live" indicator on that basis would be claiming a freshness it does
not have. Not a secret: it is a property of this deployment, and the caller already holds
a token.

noise_rules.description:
The rules that decide which messages are read automatically. `#196 auto-read-noise`.

Here rather than behind a route of its own because the page needs them at startup, for the
Settings editor, and every device and the voice agent share one list. Absent from an older
server — the page then hides the editor — and also when this one cannot read its store, so
a broken store makes the editor disappear rather than show a list that is not in force.

owner_author_id.description:
The READER's own Discord account, when the operator has said what it is.

Distinct from `self_author_id`, which is the BRIDGE's account and is read out of the bot
token. This one cannot be derived from anything the server holds — a bot's account has no
relationship to the human reading the channel — so it is absent unless configured. The page
draws both as the owner's own words, because they are: one typed into Discord, one dictated
through this bridge.

providers.description:
Each configured chat provider and what it can do, in configuration order.

Every channel names its provider by key ([`ChannelInfo::provider`]). The deployment-wide
flags above say whether ANY provider can do something; a page showing one channel uses
that channel's provider entry here instead, so a channel read through a provider without
threads is never offered a thread view because some other provider has one.

Sent only when there are several providers. With one, and from an older server, it is
absent and the deployment-wide flags are that provider's.

read_aloud.description: Selected read-aloud backend and the playback interface the browser should use.

replay_enabled.description:
Whether a new call will be handed the earlier transcript: the operator allowed it AND the
voice backend can carry it (a `vibe-talk-v1` socket cannot; see `replay::offered`).

The page needs it BEFORE it has anything to replay: the Settings screen has to describe
what resuming will do, and the control's own note has to say what the next call will be —
both of which are questions asked while there is no conversation to fetch.

replies_in_thread.description:
Whether a reply to a main-channel message is posted in that message's thread, starting one
when it has none, because the provider has no reply pointer of its own (Slack).

`#252 thread-button-state`. Such a reply already starts the message's thread, so the reply
screen offers no separate "start a new thread" choice when this is true. Sent only when
true: absent, from this server or an older one, means false.

self_author_id.description:
The Discord account this bridge posts as, when it can be known.

NOT a secret: a bot's user id is visible on every message it has ever sent. It is here so
the channel view can tell the owner's own words -- posted on his behalf by this bridge --
from everybody else's, on the FIRST render rather than only after he has replied from the
app. `None` when the token is not in the shape ids can be read from; the page then falls
back to learning it the old way.

speech_prep_enabled.description:
Whether this server rewrites message bodies for speech before anything says them.

Here for the same reason as `replay_enabled`: Settings has to be able to describe what this
deployment does, and the page cannot infer this one from any message it holds. An empty
`spoken_content` means "the rewrite changed nothing" just as often as it means "the pass is
off" — deliberately, see [`crate::model::Message::spoken_content`] — so a page guessing from
the data would tell the operator the feature was off every time the channel was plain prose.
They are flipping this switch to compare two runs; guessing is exactly what they cannot do.

summaries_unavailable.description:
Why message summaries cannot work on this deployment at all, when the server knows.

Present means the page disables the summaries control and says this instead of letting
every long row fail one request at a time. Absent means summaries may work.

threading_supported.description: Whether the backend supports channel, thread-list, and flattened timelines.

token_scope.description:
The scope of the token that asked.

The caller's own scope, so it discloses nothing it did not already hold. The page needs it
to avoid asking for what this token cannot have: stored conversations are write-only (see
the conversation routes), and a read-scope page that probed them anyway got a 403 and a
console error on every load. `#38 read-token-conversation-probe`.

upstream_clear_supported.description:
Whether the selected provider can clear its own unread state as this server ingests
messages, for a channel the owner turns that on for. `#232 upstream-mark-read`.

Settings offers the per-channel control only when this is true. Sent only when true:
absent, from this server or an older one, means false.

upstream_read_mark_supported.description: Whether the selected provider exposes a write-through read cursor.

version.description: Server version, so a stale cached page is visible.

voice_prompt.description:
The owner's own words for the voice agent, as Settings shows them. `#272
voice-agent-instructions`.

Here so the Instructions editor is drawn at sign-in, as the send setting is. Readable at
read scope — the assembled prompt is served there too, to a bridge holding the read token —
and changed only by a write-scope `PUT /api/v1/voice-prompt`. Absent from an older server;
the page then hides the editor.

voice_settings.description:
"Ask me before the voice agent sends", as Settings shows it. `#264 voice-send-approval`.

Here so the checkbox is drawn at sign-in, as the noise rules are. Readable at read scope —
it says how the voice agent behaves, which a reader of the channels may know — and changed
only by a write-scope `PUT /api/v1/voice-settings`. Absent from an older server, which
always asked; the page then hides the checkbox.

parts.description: Every part, in order. One element for a message that fitted.

posted.description: The FIRST message as the chat service accepted it.

Description.description: Public capabilities of the selected read-aloud provider; never contains credentials.

local_only.description:
Whether browser speech must select a voice advertised as running locally.
This is the browser's `localService` flag; the device engine controls actual networking.

playback.description: Which playback interface the browser should use.

Heading.description:
What a message's first line says about it, lifted out for the row's header. `#242
rich-headers`.

Every piece is UNTRUSTED plain text out of `content`, to be drawn as text. Flat and optional
throughout, so the contract can grow without an older page refusing the row.

cut.description:
How much of `content`, from its start, the heading restates, in UTF-16 code units: the
length a page's string indexes by. Always within the first line.

tag.description: Who the message says wrote it: `build-bot coordinator`, `ops2`.

time.description: The clock time the message states, exactly as written: `10:52 PM ET`, `15:05Z`.

title.description: The short title it opens with, emphasis markers removed.

LiveDeleteEvent.description: The data of a live stream `message_delete` event: only the ids, never the removed text.

channel_id.description: Channel the message was removed from.

from_tail.description: Whether it was published before this stream attached; see [`LiveMessageEvent::from_tail`].

replayed.description: Whether it was classified as history rather than news.

LiveDelivery.description: How channel changes reach the live stream.

oneOf.description: Live ingestion is off; the stream attaches and delivers nothing.
The server polls the chat provider on an interval.
A provider-neutral adapter pushes changes to the ingest route.

LiveMessageEvent.description: The data of a live stream `message` or `message_update` event.

from_tail.description:
Whether it was published before this stream attached and is re-sent from the replay tail.
Any channel read begun after the stream's response arrived has already seen it. An
adapter's catch-up arriving after the attach is `replayed` but not from the tail: it may be
newer than every read the page has made.

message.description: The message as it now stands. UNTRUSTED: written by whoever is in the channel.

replayed.description:
Whether it was classified as history — a replay or a catch-up — rather than news. The page
may render such a message but must not announce it to a live conversation.

self_posted.description: Whether THIS SERVER posted it; the page must not relay these into a live conversation.

untrusted_content_notice.description: Standing reminder that the content is third-party text.

LiveResetEvent.description: The data of a live stream `reset` event: the subscriber fell behind the replay tail.

detail.description: What the subscriber should do instead of resuming.

missed.description: Events this subscriber missed, or `0` when the count is unknown.

Message.description: One chat message as the rest of the server sees it.

author.description: Display name of the author, as reported by the chat provider.

author_id.description:
Snowflake of the author.

This travels with every rendered message ON PURPOSE, and the alternative — a
"look up this display name" tool — was rejected. Two reasons, in order of importance:

1. **No lookup step, so nothing to guess.** The id arrives ATTACHED to the very message
   being replied to, so a caller that wants to mention its author already holds the exact
   snowflake. A lookup tool would put a fuzzy name match between the agent and a real
   notification, and a hallucinated id pings a stranger.
2. **It bounds who can be mentioned.** The only ids a caller ever sees are those of people
   and bots that have actually spoken in an allowlisted channel. A general user-lookup tool
   would let the agent ping anyone in the server, which is a strictly larger capability
   than this project wants to hand a voice model.

Bots have ids too and they are included: addressing another coding agent by mention is a
legitimate thing to want.

author_is_bot.description: Whether the chat provider flagged the author as a bot.

channel_id.description: Channel the message was read from, in the provider-neutral application namespace.

content.description: Raw message body. UNTRUSTED: written by whoever is in the channel.

content_html.description:
The body as the page draws it: `content` rendered from Markdown and SANITIZED, by
[`crate::render`]. `#217 markdown-blocks`.

A third field for the same body, and it answers a third question: not what was written
(`content`, which a copy keeps and the speech path falls back to) nor what a voice should
say (`spoken_content`), but what the reader should SEE — lists with bullets, paragraphs with
space between them, a link that is a link. HTML the server's sanitizer has already cut to a
small allowlist, so the page inserts it as it stands and builds no markup of its own from
channel text.

EMPTY means "draw `content` as plain paragraphs", by the convention `spoken_content`
follows: it is what a message carries before anything renders it — on every path toward a
model, which has no use for HTML — and what it carries when rendering changed nothing,
which is most chat. Filled only on the routes the page reads.

heading.description:
The tag, time and title the message's first line states, for the page to show in the row's
header. `#242 rich-headers`; see [`crate::heading`].

Filled where `content_html` is, on the routes only the page reads, and absent everywhere
else, including from a message nothing could be read from. When it is set, the part of the
first line it restates is marked in `content_html` (or, for a plain body, is
`content[..cut]`), so the page can hide those words while it shows the heading and draw them
exactly as before when it does not.

noise.description:
Whether the owner's noise rules call this message read already. `#196 auto-read-noise`.

DECIDED BY THIS SERVER EVERY TIME the message is served, from its current text, by
[`crate::noise::NoiseFilter::mark`]; it is never stored and never trusted from whoever
sent the message. That is what lets an edited placeholder come back as unread, and a
removed rule un-hide everything it caught, without a single record having to change.

The page reads this flag rather than matching the text itself, so there is one predicate
and it is the server's. Absent means `false`, which is also what an older server meant.

reactions.description:
The emoji people reacted to this message with, and how many of each. `#219
emoji-reactions`.

ABSENT AND EMPTY ARE DIFFERENT ANSWERS. Absent (`None`) means this copy came by a path that
cannot see reactions: a provider that does not report them, or a live echo of a message,
which carries none. Empty means the source looked and there are none. So a live copy
without reactions never overwrites a held copy that has them — the echo of a message
arrives after the read that brought its acknowledgements — while a read replaces them, as
it replaces the rest of the message. Discord omits the array when there are none, so on
that provider absent from a read means none.

Counts only, never who reacted: that is a separate question for each emoji, and asking it
would hand this server identities it has no use for. UNTRUSTED: a custom emoji's name is
written by whoever made it.

reply_to.description:
The message this one is a reply to, when it is one.

Discord records a reply on the REPLYING message, as `message_reference.message_id`, and
nowhere else — there is no "replies" field on the message being answered. So "has this been
replied to?" is not a fact a single message carries; it is derived by looking at what else
is loaded. That derivation belongs to the reader, which is why this field is the raw pointer
and not a `has_replies` boolean:

1. **A boolean computed here would be a lie about scope.** The server answers a read with a
   WINDOW of a channel, so it could only ever mean "replied to within this window", and a
   field named `has_replies` would be believed to mean more than that.
2. **The pointer is the durable fact.** It is true of the message forever, independently of
   what else happens to be loaded beside it.

`None` for an ordinary message, and also for a reply whose reference Discord did not
include. Absent is not "not a reply"; it is "no pointer was reported", and nothing should
present the two differently.

spoken_content.description:
The same body rewritten for speech by [`crate::speakable`]: markdown off, instants said the
way a listener places them, long ids and hashes named. READ THIS ONE ALOUD.

Two fields for the same reason there are two time fields — they answer different questions.
`content` is what was written and is what the SCREEN must show, character for character;
this is what a voice should say, and saying it costs the reader none of the seconds that
spelling a nineteen-digit snowflake costs. Neither is a substitute for the other, and a
renderer that picked one for both jobs would be wrong in one of them.

UNTRUSTED, exactly as much as `content` is: rewriting a body for speech is not sanitizing it
for a prompt, and it still goes through [`crate::untrusted`] on the way to a model.

EMPTY means "the body to say is the raw body". That covers two cases on purpose: nothing has
prepared this message yet — the chat adapters hold no configuration, so [`crate::ops`] is the
only filler, the same convention as [`Message::spoken_time`] — and the prepared form came
back identical, which is the common case for ordinary chat with no markdown and no ids in
it. One value can mean both because [`Message::spoken_body`] answers them the same way, and
collapsing them is what keeps a window of a hundred messages from carrying a hundred
near-copies of itself down a phone's connection. When the field IS set, something was
genuinely rewritten.

spoken_time.description:
The same instant in the operator's configured zone, already formatted for speech: `09:51`.
READ THIS ONE ALOUD.

Two fields rather than one because they answer different questions, and because a single
field would force whoever renders it to choose — which is exactly the choice that produced
the bug. Handed an ISO string in UTC, the assistant said "thirteen fifty-one Eastern Time":
it kept the digits and relabelled them. A value that is already correct when read verbatim
requires no conversion and admits no such mistake.

No seconds and no zone label: see [`crate::clock::spoken`], which explains what carrying
them cost a listener and what dropping them trades away.

EMPTY means "not yet stamped". The Discord layer constructs it empty because it holds no
configuration and therefore does not know the operator's zone; [`crate::ops`] is the only
filler. Use [`Message::spoken`] to read it, which falls back to the exact instant rather
than to a blank.

thread.description: Thread membership supplied by the backend; independent of a reply-to message reference.

timestamp.description:
The exact instant, ISO-8601, as reported by the chat provider. Compute with this one.

Unrounded on purpose: sub-second precision is ordering information, and anything that has
to decide which of two messages came first needs it. This field is never spoken; see
[`Message::spoken_time`] for the one that is.

MessageId.description: A Discord message snowflake, as a string.

MessageThread.description: Thread membership attached to a message without conflating it with a reply reference.

id.description: Opaque thread identifier, scoped to the configured channel.

is_root.description: Whether this message is the original thread root.

reply_count.description: Number of replies, when the provider can supply it.

reply_count_exact.description: Whether the reply count is exact rather than a provider estimate.

root_message_id.description: The original channel message, if this provider exposes one.

MessagesResponse.description:
`GET /api/v1/channels/{id}/messages`: a channel's most recent messages, the window the classic
page draws.

`#208 persistent-cache` made it a contract root, appended below, when it gained `as_of`.

as_of.description:
The instant, RFC 3339, up to which the provider knows `messages` is complete, when it
served a copy it could not bring up to date just now: a bridge reading its Flat view says
so. Absent means now, and from an older server. The same field as
[`crate::threads::TimelinePage::as_of`].

complete.description:
Whether the fetch came back short, so `messages.len()` counts the CHANNEL rather than the
window this server asked for.

A client may show a message count only when this is true. Discord gives no message count
for a guild text channel, so a full window means "at least this many" and nothing more.

dismissed.description:
Which of `messages` the reader has ARCHIVED, so the view can dim them.

The ordinary channel view shows archived rows greyed rather than hidden -- hiding is what
the To do filter is for -- and it can only do that if the payload says which they are.

untrusted_content_notice.description: Standing reminder that the content is third-party text.

NoiseRules.description:
The owner's noise rules, as the Settings editor shows them. `#196 auto-read-noise`.

Also the body `PUT /api/v1/noise-rules` answers with, so the editor redraws from what the
server STORED — trimmed and de-duplicated — rather than from what was typed.

matching.description:
One sentence saying how a rule matches, written beside the matcher and quoted by the page
where the rules are edited, so the description cannot drift from what the server does.

rules.description:
The rules in force, in the owner's order and his own spelling. Until he saves a list this
is the shipped default.

PendingPost.description:
A post waiting for the owner's confirmation. `#34 voice-chat-write-confirm`.

Everything the confirmation has to show — the exact text, where it goes, what it answers — and
the handle that commits exactly this. The handle is a capability: it is handed only to a
write-scope caller of the proposal routes, never to a model, and a commit must restate the
channel, text, and reply target it was issued for.

channel_id.description: The channel it would be posted to.

channel_name.description: That channel's name as the owner knows it, alias included.

reply_to.description: The message it would reply to, when any.

serial.description: Correlates this proposal's steps in the access log. Increases with every proposal.

text.description: The exact text that would be posted.

PendingPostResponse.description: The post waiting for confirmation, or `null` when none is.

proposal.description: The pending proposal. At most one exists: a new proposal supersedes the old.

Pin.description: One pin, as the store holds it.

author.description: Its author's display name when it was pinned. UNTRUSTED.

author_id.description: Its author's id, so the row is drawn in its speaker's colour like every other row.

author_is_bot.description: Whether the chat provider flagged the author as a bot.

content.description: Its text when it was pinned, at most [`MAX_PIN_TEXT_CHARS`] characters. UNTRUSTED.

content_html.description:
The snapshot's text as the page draws it, rendered and sanitized when the pin is SERVED,
never stored. It follows [`crate::model::Message::content_html`]'s convention: empty means
"draw the text as plain paragraphs". `#217 markdown-blocks`.

heading.description:
The snapshot's heading, found when the pin is SERVED and never stored, by
[`crate::model::Message::heading`]'s rules. `#242 rich-headers`.

message_id.description: The message pinned, in the provider-neutral namespace the page was served it in.

pinned_at_ms.description:
When it was pinned, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, by this server's clock. The order
the bound drops pins in.

thread_id.description: The thread the message is in, when it is in one — what opens it in its thread.

thread_root.description: Whether the message is that thread's root.

timestamp.description:
When the message was sent, ISO-8601, exactly as the provider reported it. What the page
orders pins by, among themselves and among the messages it has loaded.

PinChangeResponse.description: What one pin or unpin did: `PUT` and `DELETE /api/v1/channels/{id}/pins/{message_id}`.

changed.description: Whether the call changed anything; false when it repeated what was already so.

pin.description: The pin exactly as stored — its text cut to the bound — or absent after an unpin.

pins_notice.description: The standing statement that these pins are this server's own.

revision.description:
The channel's pin revision after the call, so the page that made it need not read the list
again to stay current.

unpinned.description:
Pins the bound dropped to make room for this one, oldest first. Empty except at the bound,
and the page says so when it is not.

limit.description: How many pins a channel keeps before the oldest is unpinned to make room.

pins.description:
Every pin, in the order their messages were sent, oldest first, each with the snapshot that
lets the page draw it when its message is not loaded.

pins_notice.description: The standing statement that these pins are this server's own.

revision.description: The revision this list is at; see [`TimelineResponse::pins_revision`].

untrusted_content_notice.description: A snapshot is channel content, and untrusted, like every other.

Playback.description: How the web app plays messages with the selected provider.

oneOf.description: The browser speaks text using the device's speech engine.
The server returns encoded audio.

PromptDelivery.description: How the owner's words reach the voice agent. `#272 voice-agent-instructions`.

oneOf.description:
A deployment-managed bridge fetches the assembled prompt from `GET /api/v1/voice-agent` as
each call opens, so both texts reach its next call.

The page hands them to a hosted agent as each call opens: the whole assembled prompt when
the agent allows its prompt to be replaced, otherwise the instructions alone, as a note at
the start. The voice session says which ([`SessionPrompt`]).

PromptTransport.description: How the page hands the owner's words to a hosted agent. `#272 voice-agent-instructions`.

oneOf.description:
As the system prompt itself, in the initiation frame's
`conversation_config_override.agent.prompt.prompt`. Only when the agent allows it: an
override it does not allow is believed to end the conversation.

As a `contextual_update` sent right after the initiation frame. The agent keeps its own
prompt; only the instructions reach it.

Nothing: the agent does not allow its prompt to be replaced (or its configuration did not
say, or could not be read), and the owner has no instructions saved — he saved nothing, or
edited only the base prompt. The initiation frame is exactly what it always was, and the
agent keeps the prompt in its provider's console.

ProviderDescription.description: One configured chat provider, as the page needs to know it.

channel_discovery_supported.description: Whether this provider can list its channels for browsing.

channel_registration_supported.description: Whether this provider accepts pasted links and references when adding a channel.

idempotent_posts_supported.description:
Whether this provider posts a message sent again under the same key at most once. Sent
only when true.

key.description: The key channels name this provider by.

live_delivery.description: How changes in this provider's channels reach the live stream.

live_poll_seconds.description: Seconds between this provider's live polls, or `0` when it is not polled.

name.description: Human-readable name of the source chat service.

owner_author_id.description: The owner's own account at this provider, when configured.

replies_in_thread.description:
Whether a reply to a main-channel message is posted in that message's thread, starting one
when it has none, because this provider has no reply pointer of its own (Slack).
`#252 thread-button-state`. Sent only when true.

self_author_id.description: The account this server posts as at this provider, when known.

threading_supported.description: Whether this provider supports channel, thread-list, and flattened timelines.

upstream_clear_supported.description:
Whether this provider can clear its own unread state as this server ingests messages.
`#232 upstream-mark-read`. Sent only when true.

upstream_read_mark_supported.description: Whether this provider exposes a write-through read cursor.

Reaction.description:
One emoji's tally on one message. `#219 emoji-reactions`.

Flat, with optional fields, rather than a union of standard and custom emoji: the contract
grows by optional fields without an older page refusing the row, and a union's new variant
would be refused (see [`crate::contract`]).

count.description: How many reacted with it. At least one: an emoji nobody reacted with is not listed.

custom.description:
Whether `emoji` is a custom emoji's name rather than the emoji itself. A page draws a name
as `:name:`, so it reads as an emoji's name and not as a word somebody wrote.

custom_id.description:
The provider's own id of a custom emoji: a Discord snowflake, a Google Chat uid. Opaque,
never a URL and never shown; it keeps two custom emoji of the same name apart.

emoji.description:
What to show: the emoji itself for a standard one ("👀"), or a custom emoji's name without
colons ("party-parrot"), which is all of it a page can draw without fetching an image.
UNTRUSTED, and never empty.

ReplyDismissals.description:
Every message marked Done at or after one position in a channel. `#222 unread-replies`.

COMPLETE FROM `from` UP, which is the whole of its use: a message at or after `from` that is
not in `messages` is not Done, so a reply put back on another device leaves the list as surely
as one marked Done joins it. Below `from` it says nothing. A position is a message id read as a
number, which every provider here orders by time, so a reply is never before its thread's root
and every reply to a root at or after `from` is covered.

`from` is the page's oldest row, raised to the oldest mark kept when more than
[`crate::ops::MAX_REPLY_DISMISSALS`] marks lie above it: the newest are kept, because unread
replies are the recent ones. Ids and no text, as `dismissed` is.

from.description: The position the list is complete from: a message id, compared as a number.

messages.description: Every message at or after `from` that is marked Done, newest first.

SessionPrompt.description:
What the page hands a hosted agent as a call opens, so the call carries the owner's words.
`#272 voice-agent-instructions`.

On every voice session whose provider is one the page configures, whatever the owner has saved.
An agent that allows its prompt to be replaced is handed the assembled prompt on every call, so
its send rules follow the Sending switch; one that does not is told `not_sent` when nothing of
the owner's can reach it, so the page learns that the agent keeps the prompt in its provider's
console. Absent for a provider that reads the profile instead (a deployment-managed bridge), and
from an older server; the page then sends exactly what it always sent.

instructions_applied.description: Whether the owner's additional instructions are in what is sent.

override_allowed.description:
What the agent's configuration said about replacing its prompt; absent when it could not
be read or did not say, which is treated as not allowed.

system_prompt_applied.description: Whether the owner's edited base prompt is in what is sent.

text.description:
What to send: the whole assembled prompt for `prompt_override` — the shipped one when the
owner saved nothing — the heading and the instructions for `contextual_update`; absent for
`not_sent`.

ThreadSummary.description: One thread in the thread list, independent of the underlying provider's channel model.

display_name.description:
A short hyphenated name for the thread, chosen once by a summariser and then kept even if
the thread drifts, so the reader always finds it under the same name. Absent until named.

id.description: Opaque identifier used for reading or posting to this thread.

reply_count_exact.description: Whether the reported count is exact.

root.description: The original message, when available and readable.

summary.description:
One sentence on what the thread is about now, re-summarised as it grows. Absent until
summarised. See [`thread_summary_due`] for when it is refreshed.

title.description: Provider-supplied title, or a neutral fallback.

updated_at.description: Latest message activity, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.

TimelineDelta.description: What a forward read says about the changes it carries. `#203 incremental-refresh`.

complete.description:
True when this delta carries EVERY creation, edit, deletion and summary change in the view
since the cursor. False when it carries additions only: a read filtered by creation time
cannot see an edit or a deletion, which then reach the caller through live events or its
next full read.

deleted.description:
Messages removed since the cursor, channel-wide in every view. Always empty when
`complete` is false.

more.description: More changes remain past this page: ask again with `next_after` straight away.

removed_threads.description: Threads that left the thread list since the cursor. Threads view only; empty elsewhere.

TimelineResponse.description: A provider-neutral timeline plus this application's channel and read-state metadata.

as_of.description:
The instant, RFC 3339, up to which the backend knows this page is complete, when it is
serving data it could not bring up to date just now. Absent means now.

bookmark.description:
This channel's bookmark and its revision. `#240 reading-bookmark`.

On every read, newest page and delta alike, as `pins_revision` is, and for its reason: a
refresh that already happens is how a page learns the owner moved the bookmark on his other
device. ONE small row, so it rides inline rather than as a revision and a second read.
Absent when the store cannot say, and the page keeps what it has; `anchor: null` inside it
is the different answer that no bookmark is set.

channel.description: Configured parent channel, including its local alias and write policy.

delta.description:
Present exactly on an answer to `after`: the page then carries only what is new or changed
since that cursor, and rows absent from it are UNCHANGED, never deleted.

dismissed.description: Messages on this page that the reader has archived locally.

has_threads.description: Whether accessible threads exist in this channel.

messages.description: Messages for main, flat, or thread views, ordered oldest first.

next_after.description:
Forward cursor for this view: what to pass as `after` to learn what changed since this
page. `#203 incremental-refresh`.

From a backend, present only when that backend answers `after` itself. Above the backend
vibe-talk always fills it on a newest page or a delta — with its own generic cursor when
the backend left it empty — and removes it from a `before` page, which says nothing about
the newest end. Absent from an older bridge's answer, which therefore still parses.

next_before.description: Opaque continuation, present exactly when another page exists.

notice.description: Relevant provider limitation or scope information, if any.

pins_revision.description:
The revision this channel's pins are at. `#206 pin-message`.

On every read, newest page and delta alike, so a refresh that already happens is what tells
a page another device pinned or unpinned something; the page reads `/pins` again only when
this differs from the revision of the list it holds. Absent when the store cannot say — no
storage configured, or a failing one — and from an older server.

reply_dismissals.description:
`#222 unread-replies`. On the newest page of Main, or a delta of it, in a channel with
threads: every message marked Done from a position on, the replies in Main's threads
included. Absent everywhere else.

`dismissed` names only the rows on the page, and Main shows a thread's root but none of its
replies, so without this a page in Main could not learn that a reply it holds from All was
marked Done, or put back, on another device. See [`ReplyDismissals`].

returned.description: Entries on this page, never a channel-wide total.

thread.description:
The selected thread, for the thread view. Outside it, the one thread a channel registered as
a single conversation is scoped to: that channel has no child threads (`has_threads` is
false), and its main view carries the conversation's replies as well as its root.

threads.description: Summaries for the threads view, ordered by last activity oldest first.

untrusted_content_notice.description: Channel content remains untrusted data in every view.

TimelineView.description: A view of one configured channel.

oneOf.description: Messages posted directly to the channel, including thread roots.
Thread summaries, ordered by their latest message activity.
Channel messages and all accessible thread messages in one chronological history.
The history of one explicitly selected thread.

TokenScope.description: The scope of the credential that made a request.

oneOf.description: May read channel history and summaries.
May also post, and may use the write-only conversation routes.
The person on the call.
The voice agent.

UpstreamClearAttemptView.description: One push, as Settings shows it. `#232 upstream-mark-read`.

at_ms.description: When it was made, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

message_at_ms.description: That message's instant, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

message_id.description: The newest ingested message it was for.

previous.description: The provider's cursor before it, as the provider wrote it.

target.description: Where the provider's cursor was moved to, or would have been, as the provider wrote it.

UpstreamClearMode.description:
Whether the server clears one channel's unread state at its chat provider as it ingests
messages. `#232 upstream-mark-read`.

The ONE exception to "read state is ours" above, and it is one-way and opt-in per channel: with
it on, every message this server receives in that channel is also marked read in the provider's
own client, so a channel the owner reads here stops crowding his unread list there. Nothing is
ever read back, and this server's own read marks and Done state are not touched.

oneOf.description: Nothing is written to the provider. The default, and what no row means.
Everything is decided and logged as if it were on, and nothing is written to the provider.
The provider's read cursor is moved through each newest ingested message.

UpstreamClearNowOutcome.description: What happened to a press of "Mark read now". `#253 upstream-clear-polish`.

oneOf.description:
The press's push was made and the provider took it: `attempt` says whether its marker
moved, was already there, or, in a dry run, what a real push would have done.

The press's push was made and failed; `attempt.error` says why. It is retried by itself, at
`state.retry_at_ms`.

The bridge no longer holds the message the push named, so nothing was marked; the next
message that arrives is pushed.
An earlier push, or an earlier dry run, already covers the newest message. Nothing was sent.
The channel has no message that can be marked.

The channel is waiting out a failure, from before the press or of an older push that was
already on its way, and the newest message goes when the retry is due, at
`state.retry_at_ms`. Nothing was sent for the press.

The push is queued or on its way, and had not been recorded when the server stopped
waiting, at most 45 seconds after the press. The server keeps going without the page.

The channel's setting changed while the press waited (turned off, set to the other mode,
or every setting erased), or the channel stopped being one this server can clear, so the
push was not made as asked. `state` says what holds now.
The provider refused this channel; `state.unavailable` says why.

UpstreamClearNowResponse.description:
What Settings' "Mark read now" came to: `POST /api/v1/channels/{id}/upstream-clear/now`.
`#253 upstream-clear-polish`.

attempt.description:
The recorded push that answered the press, with `pushed`, `failed` and `skipped`, and with
`unavailable` when the push itself was refused: the pressed message's own, or a newer
message's, which covers it. What the press came to is said from this, never from
`state.last`, which a later push may already have replaced.

message_at_ms.description:
That message's own instant, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, when it can be read. An
attempt recorded later whose `message_at_ms` is at or after it answers the press, which is
how a page told `waiting` recognises the answer when it reads the state again.

message_id.description: The channel's newest message, the one the press asked to push. Absent with `no_message`.

state.description: The channel's state after it, as `GET .../upstream-clear` would answer now.

UpstreamClearResult.description: What one automatic upstream clear came to. `#232 upstream-mark-read`.

oneOf.description: The provider's cursor moved forward to the message.
The provider's cursor was already at or past the message, so nothing moved.
A dry run: the server worked out where the cursor would move and wrote nothing.
The provider or the bridge failed; the server retries with a growing wait.
The bridge no longer holds that message; the server waits for a newer one.
The provider cannot clear this channel at all, such as one thread of a larger space.

UpstreamClearState.description:
Whether this server clears one channel's unread state at its chat provider, and what it last
did: `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/channels/{id}/upstream-clear`. `#232 upstream-mark-read`.

Everything here is the server's own record. The provider's cursor is never read back except
as the answer to a push, so `pushed` and `last` say what this server did, not what the owner
has since read in the provider's own client.

enabled_at_ms.description: When it was turned on or to a dry run, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, while it is.

last.description: The most recent attempt of any kind.

mode.description: What the owner chose. Off unless set.

pending.description: Whether a message is waiting to be pushed.

previous_cursor.description: The provider's cursor before this server first moved it, for a manual undo.

provider_name.description: The name of the channel's chat provider, for the words on the control.

pushed.description: The newest push the provider's cursor is known to cover because of this server.

retry_at_ms.description: When the next retry is due, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, after a failure.

supported.description: Whether the channel's provider can do this at all. When false the mode is always off.

unavailable.description: Why the provider cannot do this for this channel, once it has said so.

UserId.description:
A Discord user snowflake, as a string.

Kept distinct from [`MessageId`] and [`ChannelId`] so the three cannot be passed for one
another: they are all decimal snowflakes, and a wrong one is silently plausible.

VibeTalkV1ClientFrame.description:
A JSON control frame a `vibe-talk-v1` client sends. Microphone audio travels separately, as
binary PCM at the session's input rate.

oneOf.description: Microphone frames follow.
The open microphone segment is over; the server answers with `turn_complete`.
One typed turn.

Stop the running turn. The server answers with exactly one interrupted `turn_complete`, or
ignores this when nothing is running.
End the session.

VibeTalkV1ServerFrame.description:
A JSON control frame a `vibe-talk-v1` server sends. Audio travels separately, as binary frames
of 24 kHz, 16-bit little-endian mono PCM.

A client ignores a `type` it does not know, so a new frame type is backward compatible; a
changed field of a known type is not.

oneOf.description: The session is ready. Always the first frame.

greeting.description:
Whether the agent speaks first. When true, a voice client withholds microphone frames
until the first `turn_complete`. Absent means false.

session_id.description: Provider session identifier, for connection details only.

oneOf.description: Recognised or generated speech text.

final.description:
False for a streaming hypothesis the provider may still correct. Absent means true, so
a provider that only sends finished text needs no change.

text.description: The words, or the current hypothesis of them.

turn.description:
The turn this text belongs to. A frame without one cannot be matched and is treated as
its own turn.

oneOf.description: Every accepted prompt, and every closed audio segment, ends with exactly one of these.

interrupted.description: True when an `interrupt` cut the turn short.

oneOf.description:
The provider failed. No `turn_complete` follows, so a client treats this as the end of the
session.

detail.description: Additional detail, when the provider has any.

VoiceDescription.description: Stable provider details that can be shown before a session is opened.

instance_id.description: Provider instance identifier, when one exists.

settings_url.description: Provider console for the configured agent, when one exists.

VoicePromptSettings.description:
The owner's own words for the voice agent, as Settings shows them. `#272
voice-agent-instructions`.

The body of `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/voice-prompt`, and `voice_prompt` in client-config. Both
texts join only the scope-neutral part of the prompt: what the agent can do — read, send, or
ask first — is added by the server from the caller's token and the send setting, after them.

changeable.description:
Whether this server can keep a change. False with no store configured, and when the store
cannot be read — the agent then gets the shipped prompt.

delivery.description: How these words reach this deployment's voice agent.

edited_from_version.description:
The prompt version shipped when he last saved his copy; present exactly when he has one.
Behind `prompt_version` means the shipped prompt has changed since.

instructions.description: Additional instructions, added to every call. Empty for none.

max_instructions_chars.description: The longest `instructions` a save may carry, in characters.

max_system_prompt_chars.description: The longest `system_prompt` a save may carry, in characters.

prompt_version.description: The version of the prompt this server ships.

system_prompt.description:
The base prompt in force: the owner's edited copy when `system_prompt_edited`, otherwise
the shipped one, so the editor always opens on what the agent is actually given.

system_prompt_edited.description: Whether `system_prompt` is the owner's edited copy.

agent_prompt.description:
The owner's words for the agent, for the page to hand over as the socket opens. `#272
voice-agent-instructions`.

Filled in by `GET /api/v1/voice-session` on every session of a hosted agent the page
configures, whatever the owner has saved — `not_sent` when none of his words can reach it —
so the page always learns what the call was given; a provider never sets it. A
deployment-managed bridge reads the same words from `GET /api/v1/voice-agent` instead, and
its sessions carry none.

input_sample_rate.description: Microphone PCM sample rate expected by the provider.

output_sample_rate.description: Speaker PCM sample rate emitted by the provider.

protocol.description: Wire protocol spoken on the socket.

provider.description: Human-readable provider label for connection details.

valid_for_seconds.description: Endpoint validity when the provider issues expiring URLs.

VoiceSettings.description:
Whether the voice agent must ask before it sends. `#264 voice-send-approval`.

The body of `GET` and `PUT /api/v1/voice-settings`, and `voice_settings` in client-config.

ask_before_send.description:
The value in force: true means `post_reply` proposes and the owner confirms, by a tap or by
a plain yes the voice page hears; false means `post_reply` posts at once. The owner's saved
choice, or the configured default until he makes one.

changeable.description:
Whether this server can keep a change. False with no store configured, and when the store
cannot be read — the server then asks, whatever the configured default says.
